text:
maria: Running into a typing / bundling mismatch when building the edge sample. Generics are collapsing to `any` after esbuild + isolatedModules. Repro under `samples/edge-runner`.
kevin: can you drop the tiny repro file and tsconfig here? makes triage faster.
maria: minimal handler: 
```ts
// samples/edge-runner/src/handler.ts
import { createClient } from '@redwood/inference';

const client = createClient({ key: process.env.RW_KEY });

export default async function (req: Request) {
  const out = await client.generate<{ text: string }>({ prompt: 'hi' });
  // editor shows { text: string } but runtime printing reveals missing shape
  return new Response(JSON.stringify(out));
}
```
my tsconfig: 
```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "ES2021",
    "module": "ESNext",
    "moduleResolution": "bundler",
    "isolatedModules": true,
    "declaration": true,
    "esModuleInterop": false
  }
}
```
maria: build log from esbuild bundling: `warning: Could not parse declaration files emitted by TypeScript. Falling back to any.` then runtime: `TypeError: createClient is not a function` in the deployed edge route.
jon: two likely overlapping problems: (A) our public typings rely on multiple overloads for `generate` / `embed` and that pattern is fragile with `isolatedModules` and bundlers which may drop type-only overloads; (B) we emit `module` metadata that confuses default vs named import depending on consumer's interop flags.
alex: i've seen `isolatedModules` force transpilers to require a single implementation signature. If our .d.ts only exposes overloads with no implementation signature, downstream tools sometimes produce weak inference or no emit.
kevin: options we discussed offline: 1) collapse overloads into a single generic signature that captures the common case and preserves inference; 2) ship a tiny shim `index.d.ts` that re-exports a single stable API for bundlers; 3) update sample docs to recommend `esModuleInterop: true` and `module: 'NodeNext'` for edge builders.
sophie: i'm leaning to (1) + (2). Overloads helped earlier, but the multi-target nature (CJS, Node ESM, edge/bundler) makes them brittle. We can keep internal overload helpers but publish one canonical exported signature.
sophie: sketch of canonical API: 
```ts
export function generate<T = string | Record<string, unknown>>(opts: GenerateOptions): Promise<T>;
```
jon: also add `types: { "types": "dist/index.d.ts" }` in package.json so bundlers pick the intended entry and don't follow deep imports. And a tiny note in RELEASE_NOTES explaining consumers might need to pin.
kevin: CI change: add a matrix that runs `tsc --noEmit` with `isolatedModules: true`, runs esbuild bundling targeting `browser` and `electron` or `edge` config, and a simple import smoke test for CJS/ESM. If it fails we block the release.
maria: CI just failed for my sample push: https://ci.internal/redsdk/8753 — failing types + a runtime mismatch. ci-bot: Build failed for branch `edge-typing-repro` (tests and typecheck). @sophie assigned.
ci-bot: https://ci.internal/redsdk/8753/details
kevin: @sophie can you add a small `samples/edge-runner/README.md` that lists the recommended tsconfig for edge consumers and a note on potential `esModuleInterop` caveat? Also include a one-liner to run local esbuild -> `esbuild src/handler.ts --bundle --platform=browser --format=esm`.
sophie: will open PR #2567 with: - replace outward-facing overloads with unified generic signatures - add `types/compat.d.ts` for legacy patterns - ensure package.json `types` points to a stable d.ts - update samples README + tsconfig and add CI matrix job - add a short migration snippet to RELEASE_NOTES / BREAKING.md
alex: quick test idea: run a repo-wide grep to find consumers relying on the older overload inference and ping owners. I'll script that and post results.
maria: thanks team. once the PR lands, can we run a small smoke suite against a few internal prod routes that use deep generics? i'd rather catch surprises before we ship.
jon: agreed, i'll queue a smoke run.
sophie: PR opened: #2567, tagging @kevin @jon for review. i'll drop a runnable repro in samples and a troubleshooting section for support.
maria: great — appreciate the quick turnaround :thumbsup:
